title: The staged harm's own numbers: weapon classes, who soaks what, the engine-sandbox Health (bought, 1 to 1000)
note: Ours, not the rules package's. The profile's values (raw_to_damage_dice, weapon_damage_bonus_one_hand_sword, damage_d10_difficulty, potence_damage_auto_success_per_rank, raw_to_soak_dice, soak_d10_difficulty, vampire_bashing_halves_postsoak) are read from the profile, never from here; this file holds only what the profile does not give. Every number here is SANDBOX or ENGINE_SANDBOX: a development control, not a rule, until the rules package answers.

dice.policy_note: H1 C4: each d10 +1 at or above the difficulty, -1 on a 1, else 0; net max(0, sum). The rules package calls it an invented adaptation; gate-11 is open.
dice.fractional_note: H1 C4: a fractional pool is the integer below or above it, the above with the chance of the fraction (one unit draw).

sword_one_hand.source: the profile (gate-10); the combat rules' sword add 2

sword_two_hand.source: ours: one more than the one-handed sword

dagger.source: ours: one less than the sword

stake.source: ours: as the dagger (no staking: its own contract, later)

blunt_one_hand.source: ours: a mace or a club as heavy as a sword, bashing

improvised.source: ours: a torch, a bucket, a cane swung

fists.source: ours: Strength alone, bashing (the source's punch)

arrow.source: ours: an arrow's potential is its work's dice (ranged.json's arrow_harm), no addend; lethal as a war arrow's head

claws.source: ours: our reading of the source's claws (aggravated; the combat rules name CLAW a subtype soaked by Fortitude and eligible armour); a question for the rules package

fangs.source: ours: as the claws (the combat rules' FANG); a question for the rules package

soak.source: H1 C2: soak eligibility precedes computation; a vampire soaks bashing and lethal with Stamina; ordinary Stamina does not soak aggravated (learned Fortitude does); historical humans cannot soak lethal with bare Stamina

fortitude.source: the power contract fortitude.passive (outputs soak.fortitude and soak.aggravated_permission; numerical_coefficients OPEN_UNLESS_MODULE_PROFILE_OVERRIDE) and the combat rules ('plus one Fortitude rank'), read as one soak die per rank; the profile has no value for it: a question for the rules package

potence.source: the power contract potence.passive (outputs damage.auto_successes); the combat rules' 'Potence N_auto=rank'

purchase.source: Blood and Health are both on a scale of 1 to 1000. The rules package: purchased maximum Health is a capacity bought on its own, independently of Stamina ('Buying ... independently greater Health/Blood capacity is allowed by the schema'); 100 by default for every person, every species (by design, ENGINE_SANDBOX; the package's 'flat 100-HP fixture ... proposed for E3 transaction testing')

health.maximum_source: the purchase 1:1 while the profile's health_max_purchase_curve is null (gate-17, OPEN_NUMERIC; asked), as Blood's maximum is its purchase (rules/blood). A new person is full; the current is held to the maximum when it falls, and a full pool stays full when it rises
health.hp_per_wound_source: ENGINE_SANDBOX (by design): the stages keep wounds as their unit (injury units) and convert each to 15 Health. 7 x 15 = 105 >= 100, so the default person still stops at the seventh wound (the seven-level calibration of the earlier bouts kept); buying more Health endures more of the same fixed harm ('compare same injury with different bought Hmax (absolute harm unchanged)'); the rules package's 'a deliberate wounds-to-HP translator', 'store resolved injury units and HP conversion units distinctly'. The package's HP conversion constants are OPEN

bands.source: the rules package: 'Broad candidate global status guidance was under ~25% Health injured; under ~10% severe/Crippled; zero incapacitated. Those percentages were discussed as provisional thresholds; exact onset, rounding and penalties remain OPEN.' So: labels only, below (not at) each share of the purchased maximum; no penalty reads them

health.source: the profile's health_max_purchase_curve is null (gate-17, OPEN_NUMERIC; asked). The earlier builds gave every person 7 (the combat rules' seven Health levels, 'an ordinary comparison fixture only'); the module puts Health on the 1-1000 scale chosen for it, bought as health_pool, a wound 15 of it. At nothing: the zero-Health stop (not death; no torpor, no final-death distinction: the combat rules forbid inventing those in core)
